messages.subject: Re: How to plot graph in java using renjin
messages.subject_clean: How to plot graph in java using renjin
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lalitdutt,

Most of the graphics plumbing hasn't been implementing in Renjin so you won't be able to use plot() or ggplot2.

What we generally use Renjin for is to do the computation on the server, and then send the results as json to the browser, where it can be rendered with d3.js or other tools.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: Forecasting using renjin
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lalitdutt,

it looks like your trying the use the forecast package from CRAN. Unfortunately this package is not supported in Renjin at this moment and probably will not be for the foreseeable future. This particular package uses C++ code, which we do not support. So unless you are using Renjin because your situation requires it, I suggest you use GNU R instead.

Maarten-Jan

At this time, we're focusing on compatibility with GNU R. There have been quite a few fixes / improvements / new functionality already in the master trunk. The goal is to work through as many of the issues on GitHub as possible before the Oct 15th, and then cut the next release candidate. If there's anything missing that you need right now, add it to the issue list!

All the best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: RC7 Changes
messages.body_plain:
You can use the javax.script API for this. Take a look at:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/script-engine/src/test/java/org/renjin/script/RenjinScriptEngineTest.java

to see how to invoke an R function and cast the result to the corresponding Java class. A data.frame in R is actually just a list with the class attribute "data.frame", so in Java-land, you can cast the result of a function that returns a data.frame to an instanceof org.renjin.sexp.ListVector.

The columns of the data.frame are elements within the ListVector, which you can access in java by x.getElementAsSexp(columnIndex). All data.frame columns should be instances of org.renjin.sexp.AtomicVector (the super class of IntVector, DoubleVector, StringVector, etc), which has methods that will allow you to access the individual elements (e.g. getElementAsDouble, getElementAsInt)

Note that factors in R are just IntVectors with a class "factor" and a "levels" attribute which provides labels for the integer values.

Thanks for checking it out, and yet another reminder that we *really* need to finish the java developer's guide!

Best,
Alex
